c1-esszemuveszet-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Pázmány's Prose
c1-esszemuveszet-01.scenario: At a literary evening on the Hungarian essay, you are asked why Pázmány Péter matters for Hungarian prose.
c1-esszemuveszet-01.prompt: Tell the others why Pázmány is seen as important for Hungarian prose.
cues: Say that he wrote in Hungarian
Say what his style joined together
c1-esszemuveszet-01.target: Pázmány magyarul is írt, és a népnyelvet a barokk retorikával ötvözte.
c1-esszemuveszet-01.english: Pázmány also wrote in Hungarian, and he joined the people's language with baroque rhetoric.
c1-esszemuveszet-01.canDo: I can explain why Péter Pázmány is seen as a founder of Hungarian argumentative prose.

c1-esszemuveszet-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Nyugat Essayists
c1-esszemuveszet-02.scenario: At a literary evening on the Nyugat journal, someone asks how Babits and Kosztolányi differed as essayists.
c1-esszemuveszet-02.prompt: Tell the others how Babits and Kosztolányi differed in their essays.
cues: Say what Babits's essays stood for
Say what Kosztolányi looked for
c1-esszemuveszet-02.target: Babits esszéi erkölcsi állásfoglalások voltak, Kosztolányi a pillanat varázsát kereste.
c1-esszemuveszet-02.english: Babits's essays were moral stands; Kosztolányi looked for the magic of the moment.
c1-esszemuveszet-02.canDo: I can say how Babits and Kosztolányi wrote essays for the Nyugat journal.

c1-esszemuveszet-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Learning with a Smile
c1-esszemuveszet-03.scenario: At a literary evening, a friend wonders whether Szerb Antal wrote about the classics too lightly.
c1-esszemuveszet-03.prompt: Tell your friend what you think Szerb Antal's light style was like.
cues: Say that he knew a lot
Say that his style stayed light and ironic
c1-esszemuveszet-03.target: Szerb Antal sokat tudott, de önironikusan és könnyedén írt a könyvekről.
c1-esszemuveszet-03.english: Szerb Antal knew a lot, but he wrote about books with self-irony and lightness.
c1-esszemuveszet-03.canDo: I can explain how Antal Szerb joined learning and light irony in his essays.

c1-esszemuveszet-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Europe and Home
c1-esszemuveszet-04.scenario: At a literary evening, the talk turns to Cs. Szabó László and his writing about Europe.
c1-esszemuveszet-04.prompt: Tell the others how Cs. Szabó László saw the link between Hungarian and European identity.
cues: Say that the two do not exclude each other
Say what he wrote about
c1-esszemuveszet-04.target: Cs. Szabó László szerint a magyarság és az európaiság nem zárják ki egymást.
c1-esszemuveszet-04.english: According to Cs. Szabó László, being Hungarian and being European do not exclude each other.
c1-esszemuveszet-04.canDo: I can explain how László Cs. Szabó wrote about Europe, landscape and history.

c1-esszemuveszet-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Principle of Quality
c1-esszemuveszet-05.scenario: At a literary evening, someone asks what Németh László meant by the principle of quality.
c1-esszemuveszet-05.prompt: Tell the others what Németh László meant by quality.
cues: Say what he demanded
Say what he rejected
c1-esszemuveszet-05.target: Németh László a legmagasabb igényességet követelte, a középszerűséget pedig elutasította.
c1-esszemuveszet-05.english: László Németh demanded the highest standard and rejected mediocrity.
c1-esszemuveszet-05.canDo: I can explain what László Németh meant by the principle of quality (*minőségelv*).

c1-esszemuveszet-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Five Essayists
c1-esszemuveszet-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the literary evening, you sum up what you have read about the Hungarian essay.
c1-esszemuveszet-consolidation.prompt: Sum up how two of the essayists differed.
cues: Name two writers
Say how their styles differed
c1-esszemuveszet-consolidation.target: Pázmány hosszú, barokk mondatokat írt, Szerb Antal könnyed és önironikus volt.
c1-esszemuveszet-consolidation.english: Pázmány wrote long baroque sentences; Szerb Antal was light and self-ironic.
c1-esszemuveszet-consolidation.canDo: I can describe the style of the main Hungarian essayists in a few sentences.

c1-metaforak-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Space in Expressions
c1-metaforak-01.scenario: At a language café in Budapest, a friend named Dóra asks you how Hungarian endings of place show up in figurative expressions.
c1-metaforak-01.prompt: Tell Dóra what the expression 'belemerül a munkába' shows.
cues: Say which ending the expression uses
Say how the work is pictured
c1-metaforak-01.target: A 'belemerül a munkába' kifejezésben a munka olyan tér, amelybe az ember belép.
c1-metaforak-01.english: In the expression 'belemerül a munkába', the work is a space that a person enters.
c1-metaforak-01.canDo: I can explain how Hungarian endings of place (honnan? hol? hová?) also appear in figurative expressions.

c1-metaforak-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Body Idioms
c1-metaforak-02.scenario: At a language café in Budapest, a friend named Dóra asks you what two Hungarian body idioms mean.
c1-metaforak-02.prompt: Tell Dóra what 'fejét töri' and 'szívére vesz' mean.
cues: Say what the first idiom means
Say what the second idiom means
c1-metaforak-02.target: A fejét töri azt jelenti, hogy valaki sokat gondolkodik egy problémán. A szívére vesz azt jelenti, hogy valamit nagyon komolyan vesz.
c1-metaforak-02.english: 'Fejét töri' means that someone thinks hard about a problem. 'Szívére vesz' means that someone takes something very seriously.
c1-metaforak-02.canDo: I can explain idioms with fej, szív, kéz and láb, such as fejét töri and szívére vesz.

c1-metaforak-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Landscape Images
c1-metaforak-03.scenario: At a language café in Budapest, a friend named Márta asks you what the rög and the puszta stand for in Hungarian literature.
c1-metaforak-03.prompt: Tell Márta what the rög and the puszta can stand for.
cues: Say what the rög means
Say what the puszta can mean
c1-metaforak-03.target: A rög gyakran a szülőföldhöz kötődés nehéz hűségét jelenti. A pusztát Petőfi a végtelen szabadság képeként énekelte meg.
c1-metaforak-03.english: The rög often means the heavy loyalty of attachment to the homeland. Petőfi sang of the puszta as an image of endless freedom.
c1-metaforak-03.canDo: I can explain what the rög, the puszta and the tiszta forrás mean in Hungarian cultural images.

c1-metaforak-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Border Fortress
c1-metaforak-04.scenario: At a language café in Budapest, a friend named Dóra asks you where the image of the végvár comes from.
c1-metaforak-04.prompt: Tell Dóra what the végvár image means in the national tradition.
cues: Say whom the nation defended, according to the tradition
Say where the balsors image appears
c1-metaforak-04.target: A nemzeti hagyomány szerint a magyarok a nyugati kereszténységet védték. A balsors képe Kölcsey Himnuszában jelenik meg.
c1-metaforak-04.english: According to the national tradition, Hungarians defended Western Christendom. The image of ill fate appears in Kölcsey's Hymn.
c1-metaforak-04.canDo: I can explain végvár, védőbástya and balsors as images of the national tradition.

c1-metaforak-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Digital Words
c1-metaforak-05.scenario: At a language café in Budapest, a friend named Márta asks you how new digital words fit into Hungarian.
c1-metaforak-05.prompt: Tell Márta how an expression like 'felmegyünk a netre' works.
cues: Say what the expression uses
Say what that shows about new words
c1-metaforak-05.target: A 'felmegyünk a netre' kifejezés igekötőt és ragot használ. Az új fogalmak így illeszkednek a magyar nyelvbe.
c1-metaforak-05.english: The expression 'felmegyünk a netre' uses a preverb and an ending. This is how new concepts fit into Hungarian.
c1-metaforak-05.canDo: I can explain how new digital words fit into Hungarian with existing endings and preverbs.

c1-metaforak-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Images in Hungarian
c1-metaforak-consolidation.scenario: At a language café in Budapest, a friend named Dóra asks you what you learned about Hungarian figurative images.
c1-metaforak-consolidation.prompt: Sum up for Dóra what spatial, bodily and historical images do.
cues: Say what such an image does
Name one image
c1-metaforak-consolidation.target: A fejét töri és a végvár is átvitt kép. Az átvitt kép elvont gondolatot fejez ki.
c1-metaforak-consolidation.english: 'Fejét töri' and 'végvár' are both figurative images. A figurative image expresses an abstract thought.
c1-metaforak-consolidation.canDo: I can explain spatial, bodily, landscape and historical images in Hungarian.

c1-nyelvfilozofia-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Idea of Inner Form
c1-nyelvfilozofia-01.scenario: In a reading group on the philosophy of language, you are asked what Humboldt thought a language is.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-01.prompt: Tell the group what Humboldt thought about the nature of language.
cues: Say that language is not a finished product
Say what it is instead
c1-nyelvfilozofia-01.target: Humboldt szerint a nyelv nem kész termék, hanem az emberi szellem alkotóereje.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-01.english: According to Humboldt, language is not a finished product but the creative power of the human mind.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-01.canDo: I can explain Humboldt's idea that language is a creative activity (*energeia*), not a finished product.

c1-nyelvfilozofia-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Ten Beautiful Words
c1-nyelvfilozofia-02.scenario: In a reading group on Hungarian writers, the talk turns to Kosztolányi and his list of the ten most beautiful Hungarian words.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-02.prompt: Tell the group what kind of words were on Kosztolányi's list.
cues: Say what kind of words they are
Name two words from the list
c1-nyelvfilozofia-02.target: Kosztolányi listáján rövid, érzéki szavak vannak, például a láng és a gyöngy.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-02.english: Kosztolányi's list has short, sensory words, for example láng and gyöngy.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-02.canDo: I can explain how Kosztolányi wrote about the sound and feel of Hungarian words.

c1-nyelvfilozofia-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Strong and Weak Versions
c1-nyelvfilozofia-03.scenario: In a reading group on the philosophy of language, someone asks whether the language we speak decides what we can think.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-03.prompt: Tell the group how the weak version of the Sapir-Whorf idea differs from the strong one.
cues: Say what the strong version claims
Say what the weak version claims instead
c1-nyelvfilozofia-03.target: A nyelvi determinizmus szerint a nyelv meghatározza, mire gondolhatunk; a gyenge változat szerint csak finoman irányítja a figyelmünket.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-03.english: According to linguistic determinism, language decides what we can think; according to the weak version it only guides our attention gently.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-03.canDo: I can explain the strong and the weak version of the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis.

c1-nyelvfilozofia-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Spaces and Feelings
c1-nyelvfilozofia-04.scenario: In a reading group on cognitive linguistics, you are asked to give an example of a spatial case used for an abstract idea.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-04.prompt: Give the group a Hungarian example of a spatial case used for a feeling or a relationship.
cues: Name the phrase
Say what the case suffix suggests
c1-nyelvfilozofia-04.target: Azt mondjuk, hogy kétségbe esünk, mintha egy tartályba zuhannánk.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-04.english: We say that we fall into despair, as if we were falling into a container.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-04.canDo: I can explain how Hungarian spatial cases are used for abstract ideas (*bízik valakiben*, *kétségbe esik*).

c1-nyelvfilozofia-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Language in the Digital Age
c1-nyelvfilozofia-05.scenario: In a reading group, the talk turns to whether Hungarian can stay a full language in the digital world.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-05.prompt: Tell the group what danger some people see for Hungarian and what they suggest.
cues: Say what the danger is
Say what could help
c1-nyelvfilozofia-05.target: A veszély az, hogy a magyar kiszorulhat a tudományból és a gazdaságból; segíthetnek a magyar nyelvű modellek.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-05.english: The danger is that Hungarian may be pushed out of science and the economy; Hungarian-language models could help.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-05.canDo: I can explain why some people see small and medium-sized languages as threatened by large language models and global tech.

c1-nyelvfilozofia-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Language and Thought
c1-nyelvfilozofia-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the reading group, you sum up what you have read about language and thought.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-consolidation.prompt: Sum up in a sentence or two what Humboldt, Kosztolányi and the cognitive linguists said about language.
cues: Say what Humboldt thought
Say what the cognitive linguists add
c1-nyelvfilozofia-consolidation.target: Humboldt szerint a nyelv alkotóerő; a kognitív nyelvészek szerint a téri tapasztalatok formálják az elvont fogalmakat.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-consolidation.english: According to Humboldt, language is a creative power; according to the cognitive linguists, spatial experience shapes abstract concepts.
c1-nyelvfilozofia-consolidation.canDo: I can sum up how Humboldt, Kosztolányi and cognitive linguists wrote about language and thought.

c1-tudomanyelmelet-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Knowing More Than We Say
c1-tudomanyelmelet-01.scenario: In a study group on the philosophy of science, you are asked what Polányi Mihály meant by tacit knowledge.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-01.prompt: Tell the group what tacit knowledge means.
cues: Say what we know
Say what we cannot do with it
c1-tudomanyelmelet-01.target: A hallgatólagos tudás azt jelenti, hogy többet tudunk, mint amennyit szavakkal ki tudunk fejezni.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-01.english: Tacit knowledge means that we know more than we can express in words.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-01.canDo: I can explain what Michael Polanyi meant by tacit knowledge (*hallgatólagos tudás*).

c1-tudomanyelmelet-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Core and Belt
c1-tudomanyelmelet-02.scenario: In a study group on the philosophy of science, someone asks how Lakatos Imre described a research programme.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-02.prompt: Tell the group what the hard core and the protective belt are in Lakatos's theory.
cues: Say what the hard core is
Say what the protective belt does
c1-tudomanyelmelet-02.target: A kemény mag a program érinthetetlen alapja, a védőöv pedig segédhipotézisekkel felfogja a cáfolatokat.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-02.english: The hard core is the untouchable base of the programme, and the protective belt catches refutations with auxiliary hypotheses.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-02.canDo: I can explain Imre Lakatos's idea of scientific research programmes.

c1-tudomanyelmelet-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Memory and Data Together
c1-tudomanyelmelet-03.scenario: In a study group, the talk turns to Neumann János and the computer.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-03.prompt: Tell the group what the Neumann architecture means.
cues: Say what is stored together
Say who the idea is named after
c1-tudomanyelmelet-03.target: A Neumann-architektúra azt jelenti, hogy a program és az adatok közös memóriában vannak; Neumann Jánosról nevezték el.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-03.english: The Neumann architecture means that the program and the data are in a common memory; it is named after János Neumann.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-03.canDo: I can explain John von Neumann's (Neumann János) role in computing and game theory.

c1-tudomanyelmelet-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Science and Society
c1-tudomanyelmelet-04.scenario: In a study group, a member says that science is completely free of values.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-04.prompt: Tell the group why many scholars doubt this.
cues: Say what shapes science
Say what researchers should do about it
c1-tudomanyelmelet-04.target: A társadalmi viszonyok befolyásolják, hogy mit kutatnak, ezért a kutatónak fel kell ismernie saját elfogultságait.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-04.english: Social conditions influence what is researched, so researchers must recognise their own biases.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-04.canDo: I can explain why many scholars doubt that science can be fully free of values.

c1-tudomanyelmelet-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Limits of Gene Editing
c1-tudomanyelmelet-05.scenario: In a study group, the talk turns to gene editing and its limits.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-05.prompt: Tell the group why many people ask for limits on gene editing.
cues: Name the risk
Name the principle people refer to
c1-tudomanyelmelet-05.target: Sokan attól tartanak, hogy a következmények visszafordíthatatlanok, ezért az elővigyázatosság elvére hivatkoznak.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-05.english: Many fear that the consequences are irreversible, so they refer to the precautionary principle.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-05.canDo: I can explain why many people ask for ethical limits on gene editing, AI and biotechnology.

c1-tudomanyelmelet-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Views of Knowledge
c1-tudomanyelmelet-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the study group, you compare two thinkers you have read.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-consolidation.prompt: Compare in a sentence or two what Polányi and Lakatos each stressed.
cues: Say what Polányi stressed
Say what Lakatos stressed
c1-tudomanyelmelet-consolidation.target: Polányi a személyes és hallgatólagos tudást hangsúlyozta, Lakatos a kutatási programokat.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-consolidation.english: Polányi stressed personal and tacit knowledge, Lakatos the research programmes.
c1-tudomanyelmelet-consolidation.canDo: I can compare how Polanyi and Lakatos described scientific knowledge.

c1-vitakultura-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Reform Era Views
c1-vitakultura-01.scenario: At a history club evening on the Reform Era, someone asks how Széchenyi and Kossuth differed.
c1-vitakultura-01.prompt: Tell the club how Széchenyi and Kossuth differed in the Reform Era.
cues: Say what Széchenyi wanted first
Say what Kossuth stressed
c1-vitakultura-01.target: Széchenyi először a gazdasági megerősödést akarta, Kossuth viszont a politikai szabadságot hangsúlyozta.
c1-vitakultura-01.english: Széchenyi wanted economic strengthening first, but Kossuth stressed political freedom.
c1-vitakultura-01.canDo: I can explain the Reform Era debate between Széchenyi and Kossuth.

c1-vitakultura-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Law Without Weapons
c1-vitakultura-02.scenario: At a history club evening, someone asks how Deák Ferenc resisted without weapons.
c1-vitakultura-02.prompt: Tell the club what Deák Ferenc relied on after 1849.
cues: Say what he did not accept
Say what principle he relied on
c1-vitakultura-02.target: Deák nem fogadott el hivatalt, és a jogfolytonosság elvére támaszkodott.
c1-vitakultura-02.english: Deák did not accept office, and he relied on the principle of legal continuity.
c1-vitakultura-02.canDo: I can explain how Ferenc Deák argued from legal continuity (*jogfolytonosság*).

c1-vitakultura-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Point of Order
c1-vitakultura-03.scenario: At a history club evening, the talk turns to the parliamentary debates of the Dualist period.
c1-vitakultura-03.prompt: Tell the club what obstruction was in the Dualist Parliament.
cues: Say what the opposition did
Say what it wanted to prevent
c1-vitakultura-03.target: Az obstrukció azt jelentette, hogy az ellenzék hosszú beszédekkel akadályozta a szavazást.
c1-vitakultura-03.english: Obstruction meant that the opposition blocked a vote with long speeches.
c1-vitakultura-03.canDo: I can explain what parliamentary obstruction (*obstrukció*) was in Dualist Hungary.

c1-vitakultura-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Pamphlet
c1-vitakultura-04.scenario: At a history club evening, someone asks why pamphlets mattered in Hungarian public life.
c1-vitakultura-04.prompt: Tell the club why pamphlets and newspaper polemics mattered.
cues: Say how a pamphlet spread
Say what it could influence
c1-vitakultura-04.target: A röpirat gyorsan terjedt, és hatással lehetett a közvéleményre.
c1-vitakultura-04.english: A pamphlet spread quickly and could influence public opinion.
c1-vitakultura-04.canDo: I can explain the role of pamphlets (*röpirat*) and newspaper polemics in Hungarian public debate.

c1-vitakultura-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Debate Online
c1-vitakultura-05.scenario: At a history club evening, the talk turns to debate on social media today.
c1-vitakultura-05.prompt: Tell the club what many people criticise about debate online.
cues: Name the problem with algorithms
Say what a good debate needs
c1-vitakultura-05.target: Sokak szerint az algoritmusok véleménybuborékokat erősítenek, a jó vitához viszont érvek és meghallgatás kellenek.
c1-vitakultura-05.english: Many say that algorithms strengthen echo chambers, while a good debate needs arguments and listening.
c1-vitakultura-05.canDo: I can explain how critics say algorithms and social media change public debate.

c1-vitakultura-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Three Styles
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.scenario: At the end of the history club evening, you compare three speakers you have read about.
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.prompt: Compare in a sentence or two how two of them argued.
cues: Name two people
Say how their arguments differed
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.target: Széchenyi a lassú reformokban hitt, Deák pedig a jogfolytonosságra épített.
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.english: Széchenyi believed in slow reforms, while Deák built on legal continuity.
c1-vitakultura-consolidation.canDo: I can compare how Széchenyi, Kossuth and Deák argued.

c1-jogallamisag-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Golden Bull
c1-jogallamisag-01.scenario: At a history evening in Budapest, a friend named Katalin asks you what the Aranybulla of 1222 was.
c1-jogallamisag-01.prompt: Tell Katalin what the Aranybulla was and what its resistance clause said.
cues: Say who issued it and when
Say what the resistance clause allowed
c1-jogallamisag-01.target: II. András király 1222-ben kiadta az Aranybullát. A záradék szerint a nemesek ellenszeghettek, és ez nem számított hűtlenségnek.
c1-jogallamisag-01.english: King Andrew II issued the Golden Bull in 1222. According to the clause, the nobles could resist, and this did not count as treason.
c1-jogallamisag-01.canDo: I can explain what the Aranybulla of 1222 was and what its resistance clause allowed.

c1-jogallamisag-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Historic Constitution
c1-jogallamisag-02.scenario: At a history evening in Budapest, a friend named Márta asks you what the Hungarian historic constitution was.
c1-jogallamisag-02.prompt: Tell Márta what the történeti alkotmány was and how it differed from a written constitution.
cues: Say what it was made of
Say what it was not
c1-jogallamisag-02.target: A történeti alkotmány törvényekből és szokásjogból állt. Nem egyetlen okmányban rögzítették.
c1-jogallamisag-02.english: The historic constitution consisted of laws and customary law. It was not recorded in a single document.
c1-jogallamisag-02.canDo: I can explain what the történeti alkotmány was and how it differed from a written constitution.

c1-jogallamisag-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The April Laws
c1-jogallamisag-03.scenario: At a history evening in Budapest, a friend named Péter asks you what the April Laws of 1848 changed.
c1-jogallamisag-03.prompt: Tell Péter two things the April Laws changed.
cues: Say what happened to the nobles' taxes
Say what kind of government was created
c1-jogallamisag-03.target: Az áprilisi törvények megszüntették a nemesség adómentességét. Felelős minisztérium jött létre Batthyány Lajos vezetésével.
c1-jogallamisag-03.english: The April Laws abolished the nobility's tax exemption. A responsible ministry was created under Lajos Batthyány.
c1-jogallamisag-03.canDo: I can explain what the April Laws of 1848 changed: responsible government, taxation and the end of serfdom.

c1-jogallamisag-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Constitutional Court
c1-jogallamisag-04.scenario: At a history evening in Budapest, a friend named Katalin asks you what the Constitutional Court decided in 1990.
c1-jogallamisag-04.prompt: Tell Katalin what the Alkotmánybíróság decided about the death penalty.
cues: Say who led the court
Say what it decided
c1-jogallamisag-04.target: Az Alkotmánybíróságot Sólyom László vezette. 1990-ben eltörölte a halálbüntetést.
c1-jogallamisag-04.english: László Sólyom led the Constitutional Court. In 1990 it abolished the death penalty.
c1-jogallamisag-04.canDo: I can explain what the Alkotmánybíróság did after 1989 and what it decided on the death penalty.

c1-jogallamisag-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Sovereignty and European Law
c1-jogallamisag-05.scenario: At a history evening in Budapest, a friend named Márta asks you what the debate on sovereignty and European law is about.
c1-jogallamisag-05.prompt: Tell Márta what the two sides emphasise, without taking a side.
cues: Say what the EU institutions emphasise
Say what the supporters of sovereignty emphasise
c1-jogallamisag-05.target: Az uniós intézmények a közös mércéket hangsúlyozzák. A szuverenitás hívei a nemzeti alkotmányos önazonosságot állítják előtérbe.
c1-jogallamisag-05.english: The EU institutions emphasise common standards. Supporters of sovereignty put national constitutional identity first.
c1-jogallamisag-05.canDo: I can explain what the debate between national sovereignty and European law is about, without taking a side.

c1-jogallamisag-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Turning Points
c1-jogallamisag-consolidation.scenario: At a history evening in Budapest, a friend named Katalin asks you to name the turning points of Hungarian constitutional history.
c1-jogallamisag-consolidation.prompt: Name for Katalin the years you know and what each is about.
cues: Name two of the years
Say what happened
c1-jogallamisag-consolidation.target: 1222-ben kiadták az Aranybullát. 1848-ban az áprilisi törvények felelős kormányt hoztak létre.
c1-jogallamisag-consolidation.english: In 1222 the Golden Bull was issued. In 1848 the April Laws created a responsible government.
c1-jogallamisag-consolidation.canDo: I can name the turning points of Hungarian constitutional history: 1222, 1514, 1848 and 1989.

c1-kozszolgalat-01.title: Communicative Challenge: A Data Request
c1-kozszolgalat-01.scenario: At a town information evening in Budapest, a friend named Péter asks you how a citizen can find out how public money was spent.
c1-kozszolgalat-01.prompt: Tell Péter what kind of data he can ask for and how fast the authority should answer.
cues: Say what közérdekű adat is
Say the usual deadline
c1-kozszolgalat-01.target: A közérdekű adat a közpénzek felhasználására vonatkozik. A törvény főszabály szerint tizenöt napos határidőt szab a válaszadásra.
c1-kozszolgalat-01.english: Public-interest data concerns the use of public funds. As a rule the law sets a fifteen-day deadline for a reply.
c1-kozszolgalat-01.canDo: I can explain what közérdekű adat is and how a citizen can ask for it.

c1-kozszolgalat-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Ombudsman
c1-kozszolgalat-02.scenario: At a town information evening in Budapest, a friend named Katalin asks you who can turn to the ombudsman and what he or she can do.
c1-kozszolgalat-02.prompt: Tell Katalin who can turn to the Alapvető Jogok Biztosa and what the ombudsman cannot do.
cues: Say who can turn to the ombudsman
Say what the ombudsman cannot decide
c1-kozszolgalat-02.target: Az Alapvető Jogok Biztosához bárki fordulhat. Az ombudsman nem hozhat kötelező ítéletet, de ajánlásokat tehet.
c1-kozszolgalat-02.english: Anyone can turn to the Commissioner for Fundamental Rights. The ombudsman cannot pass a binding judgment but can make recommendations.
c1-kozszolgalat-02.canDo: I can explain what the Alapvető Jogok Biztosa does and who can turn to the ombudsman.

c1-kozszolgalat-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Protecting a Whistleblower
c1-kozszolgalat-03.scenario: At a town information evening in Budapest, a friend named Márta asks what protection a whistleblower has.
c1-kozszolgalat-03.prompt: Tell Márta what the law forbids against a közérdekű bejelentő.
cues: Say what the law forbids
Say what kind of employees are meant
c1-kozszolgalat-03.target: A törvény tiltja a bejelentőkkel szembeni hátrányos megkülönböztetést és elbocsátást. A bejelentők olyan munkavállalók, akik visszaéléseket lepleznek le.
c1-kozszolgalat-03.english: The law forbids discrimination against and dismissal of whistleblowers. Whistleblowers are employees who expose abuses.
c1-kozszolgalat-03.canDo: I can explain what a közérdekű bejelentő is and what protection the law gives against megtorlás.

c1-kozszolgalat-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Digital Administration
c1-kozszolgalat-04.scenario: At a town information evening in Budapest, a friend named Péter asks what digital administration changes and who might be left out.
c1-kozszolgalat-04.prompt: Tell Péter what digital administration allows and who may be left behind.
cues: Say what can be done by phone
Say who may be left behind
c1-kozszolgalat-04.target: Ma már számos ügy intézhető okostelefonról. A digitális szakadék miatt az idősek és a kistelepülések lakói hátrányba kerülhetnek.
c1-kozszolgalat-04.english: Today many matters can be handled from a smartphone. Because of the digital divide, older people and residents of small settlements may be left at a disadvantage.
c1-kozszolgalat-04.canDo: I can explain what the Ügyfélkapu+ and the DÁP are for, and that these names change over time.

c1-kozszolgalat-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Civil Watchdogs
c1-kozszolgalat-05.scenario: At a town information evening in Budapest, a friend named Katalin asks what the TASZ and K-Monitor do.
c1-kozszolgalat-05.prompt: Tell Katalin what independent civil organisations do about public money.
cues: Name one organisation
Say what they work on
c1-kozszolgalat-05.target: A TASZ és a K-Monitor független civil szervezetek. Régóta dolgoznak a közpénzek átláthatóságáért.
c1-kozszolgalat-05.english: The TASZ and K-Monitor are independent civil organisations. They have worked for the transparency of public money for a long time.
c1-kozszolgalat-05.canDo: I can explain what civil society organisations such as TI, K-Monitor and the TASZ do to oversee public affairs.

c1-kozszolgalat-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Redress in Practice
c1-kozszolgalat-consolidation.scenario: At a town information evening in Budapest, a friend named Péter asks how a citizen can seek redress.
c1-kozszolgalat-consolidation.prompt: Tell Péter three ways a citizen can seek transparency or redress.
cues: Name the data right
Name the ombudsman and the whistleblower
c1-kozszolgalat-consolidation.target: A közérdekű adat megismerése mindenkit megillet. Az ombudsman ajánlásokat tehet, a bejelentőket pedig védi a törvény.
c1-kozszolgalat-consolidation.english: Everyone is entitled to learn public-interest data. The ombudsman can make recommendations, and the law protects whistleblowers.
c1-kozszolgalat-consolidation.canDo: I can explain how a citizen can ask for public-interest data (közérdekű adatigénylés).

c1-pestiironia-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Pesti Vicc
c1-pestiironia-01.scenario: At a coffeehouse in Budapest, a friend named Katalin asks you what the pesti vicc was and why people told such jokes.
c1-pestiironia-01.prompt: Tell Katalin what the pesti vicc was and why it mattered.
cues: Say what kind of humor it was
Say why people told such jokes under dictatorship
c1-pestiironia-01.target: A pesti vicc fanyar, szellemes poén volt. Sokak szerint a diktatúrában a szellem önvédelme volt.
c1-pestiironia-01.english: The pesti vicc was a wry, witty punchline. Under dictatorship it was the mind's self-defense.
c1-pestiironia-01.canDo: I can explain what a pesti vicc is and why people told such jokes under dictatorship.

c1-pestiironia-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Karinthy's Parodies
c1-pestiironia-02.scenario: At a Budapest coffeehouse, a friend named Márta asks you what Karinthy's Így írtok ti is.
c1-pestiironia-02.prompt: Tell Márta what kind of book Így írtok ti is and what Karinthy did in it.
cues: Say what kind of book it is
Say what Karinthy imitated
c1-pestiironia-02.target: Az Így írtok ti stílusparódia. Karinthy a kortárs írók stílusát utánozta és eltúlozta.
c1-pestiironia-02.english: Így írtok ti is a stylistic parody. Karinthy imitated and exaggerated the style of his contemporary writers.
c1-pestiironia-02.canDo: I can say what Karinthy's Így írtok ti is and why it is a parody.

c1-pestiironia-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Cabaret on Stage
c1-pestiironia-03.scenario: At a Budapest coffeehouse, a friend named Péter asks you who Géza Hofi was and what he did on stage.
c1-pestiironia-03.prompt: Tell Péter who Hofi was and what he did on stage.
cues: Say where he performed
Say what his asides did
c1-pestiironia-03.target: Hofi Géza a Mikroszkóp Színpadon is fellépett. A kiszólásaival kimondta azt, amit sokan csak otthon mertek megjegyezni.
c1-pestiironia-03.english: Géza Hofi also performed at the Mikroszkóp Stage. With his asides he said what many people only dared to remark at home.
c1-pestiironia-03.canDo: I can say who Endre Nagy and Géza Hofi were and what political cabaret did on stage.

c1-pestiironia-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Reading Between the Lines
c1-pestiironia-04.scenario: At a Budapest coffeehouse, a friend named Anna asks you how audiences understood plays under censorship.
c1-pestiironia-04.prompt: Tell Anna how a historical drama could carry a hidden message.
cues: Say what the play seemed to be about
Say what the audience did
c1-pestiironia-04.target: A darab a török időkről szólt. A közönség a sorok között olvasott, és értette az áthallást.
c1-pestiironia-04.english: The play was about the Turkish times. The audience read between the lines and understood the allusion.
c1-pestiironia-04.canDo: I can explain what ezópusi nyelv is and how audiences read between the lines.

c1-pestiironia-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Memes and the Pesti Vicc
c1-pestiironia-05.scenario: At a Budapest coffeehouse, a friend named Gergő asks you whether memes continue the pesti vicc.
c1-pestiironia-05.prompt: Tell Gergő how a meme is like a pesti vicc.
cues: Say how fast memes spread
Say what many people think about the link
c1-pestiironia-05.target: A mém gyorsan terjed, mint a pesti vicc. Sokak szerint a mém a pesti vicc folytatása.
c1-pestiironia-05.english: A meme spreads quickly, like the pesti vicc. Many people think the meme is the continuation of the pesti vicc.
c1-pestiironia-05.canDo: I can explain how many people see internet memes as the continuation of the pesti vicc.

c1-pestiironia-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Urban Wit Then and Now
c1-pestiironia-consolidation.scenario: At a Budapest coffeehouse, a friend named Katalin asks you to sum up how Budapest used humor.
c1-pestiironia-consolidation.prompt: Sum up for Katalin what jokes, cabaret and parody did under dictatorship.
cues: Say what jokes and cabaret did
Say whom you name from Karinthy to today
c1-pestiironia-consolidation.target: Sokak szerint a pesti vicc és a kabaré a diktatúrában a szellem önvédelme volt. Hofi a színpadról gúnyolta a hatalmat, ma a mémek a közösségi médiában teszik ugyanezt.
c1-pestiironia-consolidation.english: Under dictatorship the pesti vicc and cabaret were the mind's self-defense. From Karinthy through Hofi to memes, laughter was a way of lampooning power.
c1-pestiironia-consolidation.canDo: I can explain the part that jokes, cabaret and parody played under dictatorship.
